title: Fix lazy loading in webpack
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

Replace URL imports for lazyloading with  function call.

```ts
import mermaid from 'mermaid';
import mindmap from '@mermaid-js/mermaid-mindmap';

await mermaid.registerExternalDiagrams([mindmap]);
```

Resolves #3757

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

Now diagrams can be bundled during development and dependency management is much easier.

### :clipboard: Tasks

Make sure you

- [x] :book: have read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] :computer: have added unit/e2e tests (if appropriate)
- [ ] :bookmark: targeted `develop` branch

```suggestion
  "version": "9.2.1-rc.1",
```

Two issues:

- should this be v9.2.1?
- also, we need to put a `.` between `rc` and the number, because otherwise it's sorted alphabetically and not numerically. I had this issue with `9.2.0-rc10 < 9.2.0-rc9`. See the Semver spec: https://semver.org/#spec-item-9
comments.label_reasoning: The version string has incorrect formatting (missing dot in RC pre-release tag) which violates Semver spec and causes incorrect sorting, and may also have the wrong version number.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
Should we rename this to `registerLazyDiagrams()`?

Calling it `registerExternalDiagrams` sounds quite similar to the `registerDiagram` function we already have in the `mermaidApi`, but they work differently, since `registerDiagram` expects the diagram to already be loaded.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body:
I'm not sure if we want to allow 2 different methods to do the same thing (Loading external diagrams).
Exposing the internal `registerDiagram` might make our lives harder if we want to refactor stuff.

I'd suggest not exposing `registerDiagram` at all for now, see the feedback, and if there are any valid usecases, tweak the `registerExternalDiagrams` to accept non lazy diagrams and skip the internal `import`.

As the internal `import` is the recommended way to facilitate code splitting, it should be supported in most/all bundlers no?

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
> As the internal `import()` is the recommended way to facilitate code splitting, it should be supported in most/all bundlers no?

Dynamic imports are complicated (see #3757).

I'm guessing that some bundlers might be able to see that the dynamic import has a constant string, so `import("string here not a variable")` can be turned into an eager import/bundled, but I haven't tested it yet.

For `mermaid-cli`, we'd probably need to get bundle all of the ESM code into a single file `bundle.html` file for puppeteer CORS issues. But I guess even if we have this issue, I guess we can just do something like:

```js
  await mermaid.registerExternalDiagrams([
    {
      id: mindmap.id,
      detector: mindmap.detector,
      loader: async () => mindmapDiagramEagerLoaded,
    }
  ]);
```

I'll need to test this once I have time. It can always go into a future PR if we do need to fix anything!

When exposing .esm (single file)

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
We should expose `.core`, so that Webpack/ESBuild/Vite can decide how to bundle d3/khroma/other dependencies.

The `.esm` is bigger because it contains `d3`/`khroma`, but that's usually bad, since if you are using `mermaid.esm.mjs`, `mermaid-mindmap.esm.mjs`, `mermaid-xxxxx.esm.js`, you're downloading `d3` 3 times. (using `.core` means that a bundler can replace it with a single `d3` download)

(it also means users can update their dependencies if there are any security issues)
